title: A pick for every open Hotspawn CS2 fixture: 19 of 19 priced at 2026-10-26T00:59Z, including nine cards the deployed page had not collected
detail: A fresh runner collection (2026-10-26T00:58:22Z) and origination (00:58:36Z) resolved all 19 fixtures the Hotspawn lobby was offering with both win probabilities, one named side and a source link: 7 from Polymarket, 3 from Thunderpick, 1 median of Thunderpick and Bovada, 7 from the official Valve rating table and 1 from our own bo3.gg results fit. Nine of them (1079201, 1079202, 1079203, 1081159, 1081160, 1081162, 1081163, 1081164, 1093218 - NODWIN Clutch Series #13 and CCT Europe Series #12) were open on Hotspawn but absent from the snapshot the site was serving at 00:59Z; the four-hour publisher collected and deployed all of them at 01:04:20Z (inventory 81, upcoming 19, 17 featured picks, 2 researched-only, complete list 19/19 - re-read from /snapshot.json and /data/origination.json at 01:22Z). No Hotspawn crowd percentage and no HLTV fan vote enters any number. Full per-fixture table, response hashes and observation times: data/research/500519ba/coverage.json.

title: The published snapshot omitted 9 of the 19 open Hotspawn fixtures at the 00:59Z observation
detail: Between the 23:03:48Z publish and 00:59Z, Hotspawn added the new week's NODWIN Clutch Series #13 and CCT Europe Series #12 cards. The published snapshot at that minute listed 10 open fixtures; the cache-busted lobby and the fixture API agreed on 19, and the fresh ladder priced all 19. The nine missing IDs are 1079201, 1079202, 1079203, 1081159, 1081160, 1081162, 1081163, 1081164 and 1093218. Closed by the four-hour publisher: its 2026-10-26T01:04:20Z snapshot carries inventory 81 / upcoming 19 (17 featured picks, 2 researched-only, 19/19 in the complete list), and the nine are all present. The finding is kept because it is the exact window in which the site cannot yet show a pick for a new match - a reader between publishes sees the previous card set - and that bound is the four-hour cadence the brief allows.

title: HLTV answered HTTP 403 to the runner on both /matches and /ranking, so HLTV can only inform a pick from an earlier first-party capture
detail: The brief asks for HLTV to be tried first on fixtures the featured market line cannot price. At 2026-10-26T00:59:16Z the runner read https://www.hltv.org/matches and https://www.hltv.org/ranking/teams and both returned HTTP 403 (5,626 and 5,665 bytes of refusal HTML, hashed in coverage.json). The origination ladder keeps the HLTV world-ranking rung, but it can only use a captured ranking page younger than 14 days, so on this run the low-tier picks came from the official Valve rating table and our own bo3.gg results fit instead. A 403 is a limitation of this runner, not evidence that HLTV publishes no ranking for these teams.

title: EGamersWorld refused the runner and Thunderpick's public feed returned a 50-byte body while its per-match prices still joined
detail: Observed 2026-10-26T00:59:17Z: https://egamersworld.com/counterstrike/matches answered HTTP 403 (5,775 bytes), and https://thunderpick.io/api/matches answered HTTP 200 with a 50-byte body. Three fixtures were nevertheless priced from Thunderpick quotes (1079202, 1079203, 1082859) and one from a Thunderpick+Bovada median (1093218), which means the collector's own Thunderpick path read a different, populated surface; the empty body above is that endpoint answering a plain GET without the client's parameters. Neither observation is treated as proof that a market is missing: the publishable rule remains that an unreadable source adds no price and no default.

title: The Hotspawn fixture API rejects the cache-buster query parameter that the lobby pages accept
detail: Both rendered lobbies were read with a unique cb parameter and answered X-Cache MISS with Age 0 (309,942 and 309,003 bytes). The same parameter on the scheduled-fixture API returned HTTP 400 with an 83-byte body at 00:59:14Z, so the API cannot be cache-busted this way; it was read once, unmodified (63,325 bytes, 81 CS2 records), and reconciled against both rendered pages - 19 linked cards, none present only in the page, inventory crosscheck complete. Anyone re-running the audit should expect the 400 and must not read it as an empty inventory.

title: HOTU vs The Huns: the featured row in snapshot.json is blank while the complete list carries 87.0% / 13.0% from the same market
detail: In the 2026-10-25T23:03:48Z snapshot, fixture 1082792 carried analysis=null, so the featured table showed it as explicitly unresolved, while data/origination.json priced it at 87.0% HOTU / 13.0% The Huns from a Polymarket book and the rendered page showed that researched row. The 2026-10-26T01:04:20Z snapshot has two such researched-only rows (featured picks 17 of 19; complete list 19 of 19). A reader comparing the two downloads sees one fixture described two ways. Nothing is averaged or re-priced: both numbers keep their own source links, and the reconciliation is stated on the page. The Valve identity for 'The Huns' stays ambiguous on purpose (two rosters share the name, #122 and #213), so the ranking rung is not used for this fixture.

title: The 01:04:20Z publish would have frozen the next four-hour refresh: the publisher's own regression gate read a documented money-backed upgrade as a hard failure
detail: scripts/build.py::selected_fallback deliberately shows a labelled money-backed researched estimate in place of a lowest-rung model row. On the 2026-10-26T01:04:20Z publish that applies to fixture 1093218 (Nuclear TigeRES vs UNiTY): the snapshot's featured model gives 70.7%/29.3% while the page shows the published consensus of independent money sources at 58.3%/41.7% on the same side. scripts/22a3ed80_verify.py compared every rendered row with the snapshot's own analysis block only, so tests/test_22a3ed80_verification.py failed in the Validate-dashboard run (job 121351532885, step 'Test strict identity, pricing, fallback and failure handling'). That test is the first step of .github/workflows/pages.yml, which runs it before every collect, so the 03:17Z refresh would have gone red and the site would have stopped updating - the same failure class as the 824A-5 and 824A-6 fix-forwards. Fixed forward here: the verifier now requires the rendered numbers to be exactly the published origination row's (same side, same two percentages, method in market/bookmaker/consensus/reference, upgraded_from_featured_model true) before treating the difference as documented, and still fails on any other divergence. Five new tests pin both directions (tests/test_500519ba_upgrade_rule.py); the gate on the live publish now reports 15 hard checks, 0 failures, and tests/test_22a3ed80_verification.py passes 14/14.
